intro: The WHO Growth Chart Calculator lets clinicians plot a child's measurements against the WHO Child Growth Standards 2006 for children aged 0–5 years, with separate charts for boys and girls. It covers weight-for-age, length/height-for-age, head-circumference-for-age, and BMI-for-age (all 0–5 years), plus weight-for-length (0–2 years) and weight-for-height (2–5 years). The screen is a selection hub that routes to a dedicated chart-plotting view for whichever parameter and sex is chosen.
indications: Assessing a child's growth trajectory against WHO international standards from birth to age 5
Screening for undernutrition or overnutrition using weight-for-length/height or BMI-for-age
Monitoring head circumference growth for signs of micro- or macrocephaly
Tracking longitudinal growth (weight, length/height) at routine well-child visits
Comparing growth parameters against sex-specific WHO percentile curves
method: The screen offers six chart types per sex — Weight for Age, Length/Height for Age, Head Circumference, and BMI for Age (each 0–5 years), plus Weight for Length (0–2 years) and Weight for Height (2–5 years) — and hands off to a chart screen that plots the child's data against WHO percentile/z-score curves. The app displays the citation "WHO Child Growth Standards 2006" on the chart selection screen, and the underlying chart screen repeats "WHO Child Growth Standards 2006" / "WHO Growth Standards 2006" on its plotted views and PDF export.

faqs.q: What age range do the WHO charts in the app cover?
faqs.a: 0–5 years for weight-for-age, length/height-for-age, head circumference, and BMI-for-age; weight-for-length is scoped to 0–2 years and weight-for-height to 2–5 years.

faqs.q: What growth standard is this based on?
faqs.a: The app labels it "WHO Child Growth Standards 2006" on both the chart selection screen and the plotted chart views.

faqs.q: Are the charts different for boys and girls?
faqs.a: Yes — the selection screen has separate boys and girls sections, each offering the same six chart types.

faqs.q: Which chart should I use for a 4-month-old's weight relative to length?
faqs.a: Weight for Length, which the app scopes to 0–2 years.

faqs.q: Does the app support BMI tracking for young children?
faqs.a: Yes, BMI for Age is offered for children 0–5 years.
